core_obligations: Reduce to showing that the fibre product with a test scheme is a scheme, and further to showing this for its quasi-compact open subspaces (proof lines 2387-2393).
Write the source as a filtered colimit of affine schemes and factor the restriction of the projection to such a subspace through a stage (proof lines 2390-2396).

Show that the resulting morphism into a product of that stage with the test scheme is a monomorphism, hence separated, and locally quasi-finite, using permanence of local quasi-finiteness under base change (proof lines 2396-2402).

Conclude that each quasi-compact open subspace is a scheme by the criterion for locally quasi-finite separated algebraic spaces, and then that the fibre product itself is a scheme (proof lines 2402-2409).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to quasi-compact open subspaces of the fibre product (proof lines 2387-2393).
Factorisation through a stage and the monomorphism property (proof lines 2390-2400).
Local quasi-finiteness and the criteria (proof lines 2396-2409).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a map of presheaves on the fppf site whose source is an affine formal algebraic space and which is representable by algebraic spaces and locally quasi-finite is representable by schemes (statement lines 2380-2385). The proof tests against a morphism from a scheme: it has to show that the fibre product is a scheme, and it does so on quasi-compact open subspaces. Writing the source as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the restriction of the projection to such a quasi-compact open subspace factors through one of the stages, and the resulting morphism into a product of that stage with the test scheme is a monomorphism, hence separated, and locally quasi-finite because the given map is; the criterion for a locally quasi-finite separated algebraic space over a scheme then makes each quasi-compact open subspace a scheme, and a criterion for being a scheme in terms of quasi-compact open subspaces finishes the argument (proof lines 2387-2409). The claim is H2: the reduction to quasi-compact open subspaces, the factorisation through a stage, and the two criteria applied at the end are all displayed, and the local quasi-finiteness hypothesis enters exactly once, in the middle step.
